evidence: carrot, celery, cucumber and pepper are one measure, the gross profit in dollars per acre ("Gross profit for 4 vegetable crops in 6 years"), of four crops as columns, one row per year; the example stacks them as one "yearly profit by crop" in xyplot(carrot+celery+cucumber+pepper ~ year), and agridat holds no year x crop long form.

"The same test plots were used in 1953 and in 1952", so each corn plot, its replicate with its 1952 P and N levels (rep:P:N), holds a corn row (1952) and a corn2 row (1953), the absent treatment combinations the same in both years; the page's lm fits each year separately, and the alfalfa and clover plots hold one row each.

MTD to MTA, mTD to mTA, mTUD to mTUA, PRD to PRM, SHD to SHF and EVD to EVA are six weather measures with one column per month from December to April, one row per year, as UStemp's monthly temperatures; the long form is year x month, which agridat does not hold, and plsr(Z~U) takes the columns as each year's covariates.

Manufacturer indexes the make that the car models, "selected at random from among 1993 passenger car models", repeat within, most makes holding several; Model and Make are per-row ids, Origin is constant within a make, and MASS's only model, loglm(~ Type + Origin) on xtabs counts in loglm.Rd, has no row-level response.

dp/tp (placebo) and da/ta (Aspirin) are the deaths and totals of each trial's two arms as columns, one row per trial of the meta-analysis; binomial counts are each arm's whole data, so they stack into the trial x arm long form as BCG's arms do, and HSAUR3 holds none.

housing, food, goods and service are each household's expenditure in Hong Kong dollars on "four commodity groups" as columns, one row per household, one measure across targets as BEPS's leader ratings; the exercise asks how "the division of household expenditure between the four commodity groups" depends on total expenditure and gender, which the household x commodity long form holds.

qt/tt (treated) and qc/tc (control) are the quitters and totals of each trial's two arms as columns, one row per study; Ch_meta_analysis pools them by meta.MH and meta.DSL exactly as it pools BCG's arms, and the binomial counts stack into the study x arm long form.

low and high are each student's results on "two parallel forms of a test" as columns, one row per student, and treatment (AA, C, NC) is the randomized between-student factor; the long form is student x form, and the exercise's test of "the bivariate means" takes both forms jointly.

Study never repeats, and nA/meanA/sdA and nB/meanB/sdB are the size, mean and SD of the DMFS change in each trial's two arms, summaries of different subjects that stack into arm summaries, not observations, as kieseppa_2026_osf's arm columns; the example only prints the table and no file of HSAUR3 fits a model to it.

method1 and method2 are one sea state's bending moment under each mooring method as columns ("the same sample of sea states with each of two mooring methods"), one row per sea state; the long form is sea state x method, and Ch_simple_inference's t.test(mooringdiff) takes their difference.

u and x are one city's population in 1920 and 1930 as columns, the cities "a random sample taken from the 196 largest cities in 1920"; boot's examples take the ratio and the correlation of the two columns, and the long form is city x year.

baseline and oneyear are each patient's CD4 count "on admission to the trial" and "after one year of treatment" as columns, one row per patient; the long form is patient x occasion, and boot's cd4.nested bootstraps the two columns' correlation.
entry and week are each smoker's carbon monoxide transfer factor "on entry to hospital and then again after 1 week" as columns, one row per smoker; the long form is smoker x occasion.

Columns 0 to 5 are one replicate's successive firing times aligned on the stimulus (column 2 the last firing before it, column 3 the first after), "Each row of the matrix is a replication of the experiment", missing where a replicate fired less often; the long form is replicate x firing, which boot does not hold.

The rows repeat within cores ("Twelve core samples from petroleum reservoirs were sampled by 4 cross-sections"), but no column indexes the core: only the response perm, measured once per core, marks it, and a response is no grouping factor, as openml_378's unindexed households; ppr(log(perm) ~ area1 + peri1 + shape) in stats' ppr.Rd has no random effect.
